description:
In relay_client.rs load_fresh_policy(), the cache TTL is set as: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(policy.max_age as u64). When max_age=0 (a valid RFC 8461 value), valid_until equals Instant::now() at insert time, meaning the cache entry is immediately stale. On every subsequent delivery to that domain, the cache check (Instant::now() < *valid_until) is false, causing a cache miss, triggering a DNS TXT lookup + HTTPS policy fetch for every delivery.

A remote domain publishing max_age=0 can force the sending MTA to re-fetch its policy on every outbound message, causing amplified DNS and HTTPS load. With high delivery volume this degrades performance and could exhaust connection pool resources.

Fix: impose a minimum effective TTL (e.g., 60 seconds) regardless of the published max_age value. This bounds the re-fetch rate while still respecting the spirit of short max_age values. Document the floor in a comment referencing this security consideration.

Severity: P2 — reliability/security: remote-controlled DoS amplification on the fetching MTA.
title: relay_client: max_age=0 causes unbounded re-fetch on every delivery
